hypothesis: A stock's next-quarter return rises with the residual past-month return of its linked firms, falls with large section-level changes in its own filings, and rises after opportunistic insider purchases, because each is slow, indirect information; the equal-weight composite of the three adds alpha to the reference book at 2x cost. Evidence grade B-, set by the Filing Change component.
universe: US common stock, price at least $5, 60-day median dollar volume at least $10M, market cap at least $500M, links from at least two different edge sources, excluding the 100 largest firms; the short side also needs market cap of at least $1B, the broker borrow flag and the short crowding filter (risk.md)
signal: Month-end close, point in time. Components: link propagation (edge-weighted mean of linked firms' past-month residual returns; edges from customer and supplier disclosures, the 10 nearest 10-K text peers and 13F common ownership, equal-weighted across sources), section-level Filing Change (deterministic similarity of each 10-K and 10-Q to its prior-year counterpart, Item 1A and MD&A) and opportunistic insider purchases (open-market Form 4 buys in the trailing month, zero where no event fires). Each component is winsorized, ranked to a z-score and residualized against market beta, size, industry and the firm's own trailing one-month return (math.md, Composite score). Score = (z_link + z_filing + z_insider) / 3, a missing component is 0, no weight is fitted. Agreement gate: a candidate is dropped when any single component contradicts the composite's sign by more than the registered threshold (one standard deviation). Short vetoes: distress, no broker borrow flag or failing the crowding filter, concentrated forced-seller exposure from the 13F edges, market cap below $1B. Tranches: signal from the month-end close, trades the next session, monthly tranches with a 3-month hold (one third of the book re-ranked each month). Sizing: proportional to score magnitude with a single-name cap, at least 15 names a side (20 planned), 150% gross, 10% annual volatility target through the capped exposure scaler (math.md, Exposure scaler), absolute beta to VTI at most 0.3. Exit: signal exit at the rebalance with a broker-native GTC catastrophe stop at 3 x the 20-day ATR. Costs: the costs model at 1x and 2x with the borrow stress grid. Evaluation window from 2016, the free feed's start. Model involvement: none. The first harness output is the correlation matrix of the three component scores and the effective signal count, computed on the evaluation window excluding the holdout, before any Sharpe, return or spanning result.
diagnostics: drop-one ablation: no filing change component

holdout.rule: untouched holdout, never used for any choice; the longer of the last 3 years and the last 25% of the sample (proposed); seen-window: the 2016-2026 window was already seen by an earlier long-only trend test, so any run that touches the trend scaler is labeled seen-window in its report and the shadow gate minimum doubles to 6 rebalances; the scaler is judged by its no-scaler diagnostic run, never as standalone evidence

open_questions: universe: the point-in-time list is built at registration; customer and supplier edge coverage by year is measured first, and the book registers without edge (a) if coverage collapses.
holdout.end: the last real bar on disk if earlier than 2026-10-04; holdout.start moves with it.

single-name cap 6%, no-trade band 20%, scaler as in strategy/etf_trend.py and the distress veto (going-concern language or Altman Z below 1.8 where computable) are approved values; the registration records them.
